segments.title: Chương 266: 0268
segments.content:
ByteDance wasn't the only company working on mobile Weibo.

There was also the sole mobile portal website at the time, Kongzhong Corporation. But they didn't call it "microblog"; they coined their own term, "mobile blog."

Whether it was mobile Weibo or mobile blog, the functions were nearly identical.

If Chen Guiliang hadn't appeared, judging by the launch date of Kongzhong's mobile blog, it would have definitely preceded the Americans' creation of Twitter.

Kongzhong Corporation had also sent reporters to this year's China Internet Conference, and they even had their own press seats.

They broadcasted live text and images from their mobile phones throughout the event. Besides publishing news on Kongzhong's WAP site, they also sent it directly to mobile blog users' phones via SMS and MMS.

"Chen Guiliang, founder of ByteDance and Game Science, rebuts Baidu's Robin Li point by point at the conference's main forum... Robin Li, looking displeased, storms out of the venue."

This was the content Kongzhong sent out via its mobile blog. At least 300,000 users received the text message on their phones!

Yes, Kongzhong's mobile blog users had already surpassed 300,000.

In contrast, Hainei's mobile Weibo only had a little over 70,000 users.

Because Kongzhong had been a mobile website from the start, all its users were accustomed to browsing the internet on their phones. The conversion rate to their mobile blog was extremely high, and the conversion was very fast.

Hainei, however, wasn't doing so well. Most of its users were used to accessing the internet on computers, making the conversion to mobile Weibo a laborious process.

Guo Zhendong was one of Kongzhong's mobile blog users.

Due to his work, he was often away on business trips, either on a train or a plane, with very little time to use a computer.

Lying in his sleeper berth, Guo Zhendong heard the SMS notification tone. He opened the message to see: "Chen Guiliang, founder of ByteDance and Game Science, at the conference's main forum..."

What was going on?

Chen Guiliang rebutting Robin Li point by point?

Immediately after, he received an MMS message. Since the train was currently traveling through the countryside, the signal wasn't particularly good. The MMS took a full minute to load.

The MMS photo had very low resolution, but it was taken up close, and one could vaguely see the unpleasant look on Robin Li's face.

In the background of the photo, Chen Guiliang was giving a speech on stage, while a grim-faced Robin Li was walking towards the exit. He was captured by a Kongzhong reporter's mobile phone as he passed the press seats.

Guo Zhendong quickly logged into Kongzhong to read a more detailed report.

But being a WAP site, Kongzhong's news articles were always brief. This was especially true for the speeches today; they were only summarized, making it difficult to know the specific details.

The more this was the case, the more curious Guo Zhendong became.

By evening, the train had arrived at the station.

Guo Zhendong first went to his hotel to drop off his luggage. When he went out for dinner, he found an internet cafe along the way.

He used the keywords "Chen Guiliang" and "Robin Li" and immediately a ton of related results popped up. It seemed Baidu hadn't deliberately filtered the incident yet.

On Sina, the officially designated media partner, there was no comment section under the relevant news article.

After reading Sina's report in detail, Guo Zhendong immediately went to the Tianya forum to see the commotion. As expected, things were already getting heated over there.

The most popular thread was titled: "Chen Guiliang vs. Robin Li, An Internet War Between Peking University Alumni!"

The thread first posted the full text of Robin Li's speech, followed by the full text of Chen Guiliang's speech. This content was available from Sina's live text and image broadcast, so it was simply copied and pasted.

After posting both speeches, the original poster commented: "This is probably the most exciting moment in the history of the Internet Conference. Chen Guiliang's temper is no joke, and his tongue is truly sharp. He showed no mercy to his own university senior!"

"First comment."

"Second."

"Selling snacks and sodas in the front row."

"Is there something wrong with Chen Guiliang? Who speaks to someone like that in public? He has no sense of occasion."

"To the person above, is Robin Li your dad? I think there's something wrong with Robin Li. Given his status in the Chinese internet world, openly badmouthing the Web 2.0 model could probably cause ByteDance's valuation to drop by tens of millions. Cutting off someone's livelihood is like murdering their parents. Chen Guiliang not laying a hand on him was already letting him off easy."

"The theme of Chen Guiliang's speech today was the future of Web 2.0. But before he even started speaking, Robin Li was already trashing his topic. If he didn't tear into him first before giving his speech, everything he said would have become a joke. Get it?"

"Hahaha, that's hilarious. Have you guys noticed? Everything Chen Guiliang said was a point-by-point rebuttal of Robin Li's speech. Chen Guiliang found a flaw in everything Robin Li said. Was Billionaire Chen on the Peking University debate team?"

"I really don't get it. Does Robin Li even think before he speaks? He doesn't even know where Baidu's market cap would rank among Japanese internet companies? And he still had the nerve to say the Chinese internet company with the highest market cap is not even one-tenth of a Japanese internet company's market cap. What's the benefit of sucking up to the Japanese like that?"

"I've seen an interview with Robin Li before. He said he interned at Panasonic. Those three-plus months at Panasonic played a crucial role in his later entrepreneurial ventures. So, it's understandable that he emotionally reveres Japan."

"Then what's with him praising Vietnam?"

"He probably saw some data on Vietnamese netizens somewhere and used it off-the-cuff to prove that the proportion of Chinese netizens is too low. If I didn't understand the statistical discrepancies, I'd easily be misled too. Billionaire Chen is the man. He gave his speech without a script, not to mention rebutting point by point with extemporaneous remarks, and it was all well-reasoned and clear. Billionaire Chen's knowledge base is just too vast!"

"Robin Li is an idiot!"

"Fuck you, person above me. Chen Guiliang is the idiot!"

"Replying to three comments up. It's not just a matter of knowledge base, but an understanding of the market. The fact that Robin Li could say online games and wireless value-added services are small industries in the global internet sector proves he pays no attention to the market at all. He doesn't even know the two main pillars of the internet industry. It's like a top-level leukemia doctor not knowing the two most effective leukemia drugs."

"I used to admire Robin Li a lot, thought he was really amazing. Now, after reading Chen Guiliang's rebuttals, I realize Robin Li's level is just so-so. What the hell was he even saying? From start to finish, he was just making assumptions, and Chen Guiliang pointed out all his mistakes."

"Chen Guiliang really knows how to be passive-aggressive. Haha, 'Young people are drowsy, it's only when you get older that you can't sleep.' He's mocking Robin Li for being old and outdated."

"I just did a Baidu search for Legends of the Three Kingdoms. The official website is clearly the fifth search result. Chen Guiliang is lying! He said it was sixth. On behalf of Robin Li, I'm going to sue Chen Guiliang for spreading rumors!"

"For a moment there, I couldn't tell whose side you're on."

"It moved up one spot, means someone didn't renew their payment."

"I'm one of the people involved in the Baidu layoff scandal. I joined Baidu years ago, and my stock options were worth over a million yuan. But just as my options were about to vest, I was fired by Baidu without reason this May, and I received no financial compensation whatsoever! I have already filed a lawsuit. I'm going to fight Baidu in court to the very end. Robin Li is a shameless capitalist who goes back on his word and tries to stiff his long-time employees out of their stock options!"

"Holy shit, is the person above for real?"

"It's real. Have you forgotten how big the Baidu layoff scandal was back in July? Over a hundred media outlets were collectively denouncing Baidu back then."

"Support the brother above in defending his rights. Bosses who withhold pay and cheat people out of their stock options are all bastards!"

Guo Zhendong sat in the internet cafe, engrossed in reading the news and the forum posts.

Having to travel for work all year round, he had developed a habit of reading news anytime, anywhere. At first, it was newspapers and magazines on the train, then browsing news at internet cafes, and last year he became a mobile news user.

After finishing that thread, he saw another one: "Wulin Alliance Leader of Web 2.0: Chen Guiliang's Battle to Fame!"

The poster of this thread claimed:
